$batch_notes: Batch 4 — entries 127-175. Priority fills: (1) 重箱 gap — currently 20 vs 35 音音, (2) number/counter 熟字訓, (3) 真+X color intensifiers, (4) 国字 as structural constraints, (5) more cross-reference chain extensions, (6) entries that test semantic heuristics at their edges.

characters.reading_note: タイ here, not ダイ (cf. 台所=だいどころ). The reading varies by compound.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Universal vocabulary. Teaching value: 台=タイ here vs ダイ in 台所. 風=フウ(on) vs かぜ/かざ(kun).
entries.real_world_context: Weather, seasonal — '台風が近づいている' (a typhoon is approaching). Essential Japan life vocabulary.
entries.trap_note: 風 reading contrast: 台風(フウ, on), 風邪(かぜ — 熟字訓), 追い風(おいかぜ, kun). Starts a 風 chain.

characters.reading_note: おい is the 連用形 stem of おう.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Clean verb-stem + noun pattern. Extends 風 chain with kun reading.
entries.real_world_context: Business/sports metaphor — '追い風が吹いている' (the wind is at our backs / conditions are favorable). Also literal sailing/cycling.
entries.trap_note: Contrast with 向かい風(むかいかぜ, headwind). Both verb-stem + 風(かぜ, kun) = 訓訓. The pattern is productive for wind-direction compounds.

characters.reading_note: かな is the compositional kun form of かね, used when 金 is the first element meaning 'metal.' Same あめ→あま pattern as 雨.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 金=かな (not かね or キン) is the compositional kun form. Same pattern as 雨=あま. Builds the compositional-kun-form concept.
entries.real_world_context: Hardware stores — '金物屋' (hardware store). Also kitchen/tools context.
entries.trap_note: Compositional kun forms: 雨→あま (雨戸, 雨具), 金→かな (金物, 金具). This is a systematic pattern where the standalone kun reading (あめ, かね) shortens or shifts when the character appears as the first element of a compound. Worth teaching as a transferable concept.

characters.reading_note: Same compositional kun form as 金物.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Same 金=かな pattern, different classification because 具=グ(on). Parallels 雨戸(訓訓) vs 雨具(湯桶).
entries.real_world_context: Hardware, construction, DIY — '金具を取り付ける' (attach hardware/fittings).
entries.trap_note: 金物(かなもの, 訓訓) vs 金具(かなぐ, 湯桶): same 金=かな, different classification. Perfectly mirrors 雨戸(あまど, 訓訓) vs 雨具(あまぐ, 湯桶). The compositional kun form stays constant — classification depends on the partner.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends 番 chain from 番組(重箱). 番号 is 音音 because 号=ゴウ(on).
entries.real_world_context: Ubiquitous — '電話番号' (phone number), '番号札' (number ticket). Daily administrative tasks.
entries.trap_note: 番 chain: 番組(ばんぐみ, 重箱) vs 番号(ばんごう, 音音) vs 番地(ばんち, 音音). 番=バン is always on. Classification depends on partner.

characters.reading_note: キン(on) here — contrasts with かな(kun) in 金物/金具.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the 金 chain with the on reading. 金=キン in financial/abstract contexts, 金=かな in concrete/physical contexts.
entries.real_world_context: Business — '金額を確認してください' (please confirm the amount). Invoices, receipts, negotiations.
entries.trap_note: 金 chain: かな(kun, metal/physical) in 金物/金具 vs キン(on, money/abstract) in 金額/金融(きんゆう). Semantic split mirrors the on/kun split. Also extends 額 chain from 額縁(がくぶち, 重箱) — 額=ガク is always on.

characters.reading_note: ま is the prefix kun reading of 真 meaning 'true/peak/mid-.' Very productive.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Starts the 真+X intensifier pattern. 真=ま(kun) as a prefix is extremely productive.
entries.real_world_context: Seasonal — '真夏の暑さ' (midsummer heat). Weather discussions, travel planning.
entries.trap_note: 真+X set: 真夏(まなつ), 真冬(まふゆ), 真昼(まひる), 真夜中(まよなか), 真っ赤(まっか), 真っ青(まっさお). All use ま(kun). This prefix is always kun regardless of what follows — a reliable prediction anchor.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Second 真+season entry. Pattern confirmation.
entries.real_world_context: Seasonal — '真冬の寒さ' (midwinter cold).

characters.reading_note: ま → まっ via 促音 before カ.
Wait — is か on or kun here? Actually, か is NOT a standard reading of 赤. The standard on readings are セキ and シャク. This is arguably a special intensifier form.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ま + か → まっか (促音). But the か reading of 赤 is itself irregular — not standard on or kun.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Looks simple but is actually a classification problem. 赤=か doesn't fit neatly as on or kun. The 真っ+color pattern may be its own morphological category.
entries.real_world_context: Expressions — '真っ赤な嘘' (blatant lie), '顔が真っ赤' (face is bright red). Very common.
entries.trap_note: The 真っ+color pattern: 真っ赤(まっか), 真っ青(まっさお), 真っ白(まっしろ), 真っ黒(まっくろ). The color readings in these (か, さお, しろ, くろ) don't all match standard on/kun classifications. This pattern may resist clean four-category classification. Honest acknowledgment.

characters.reading_note: しろ IS a standard kun reading. Unlike 赤=か, this one classifies cleanly.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ま + しろ → まっしろ (促音)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Clean 訓訓 — 白=しろ is standard kun. Contrasts with 真っ赤 where the color reading is irregular.
entries.real_world_context: Daily life — '真っ白な雪' (pure white snow), '頭が真っ白になった' (my mind went blank).
entries.trap_note: 真っ白(しろ, clean kun) vs 真っ赤(か, irregular). Same 真っ+color pattern, but classification differs. The pattern's internal consistency is weaker than it first appears.

characters.reading_note: くろ IS standard kun. Classifies cleanly.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ま + くろ → まっくろ (促音)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Clean 訓訓. Third in 真っ+color set.
entries.real_world_context: Daily life — '日焼けで真っ黒' (dark from sunburn). '真っ黒な犬' (jet-black dog).

characters.reading_note: さお is NOT a standard reading of 青. Standard kun is あお. This is an archaic/dialectal form surviving in this compound.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ま + さお → まっさお (促音)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Like 真っ赤, the color reading is non-standard. 青=さお is not in standard reading lists. Two of four 真っ+color entries resist classification.
entries.real_world_context: Expressions — '顔が真っ青' (face turned pale/white as a sheet). Shock, fear, illness contexts.
entries.trap_note: 真っ+color pattern summary: 真っ白(しろ, clean kun), 真っ黒(くろ, clean kun), 真っ赤(か, irregular), 真っ青(さお, irregular). 50% classifiable, 50% not. The pattern is learnable as a unit even though individual entries resist decomposition. Teaching recommendation: present as a set and acknowledge the irregularity rather than forcing classification.

characters.reading_note: Wait — くつ is the KUN reading of 靴. ぐつ is くつ with 連濁. So this is kun, not on. That makes this 訓訓, not 湯桶.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Clean 訓訓 with 連濁. Material+object pattern.
entries.real_world_context: Shopping, business dress — '革靴を買いに行く.' Professional attire discussions.
entries.trap_note: I initially misclassified this — mistaking ぐつ for an on reading when it's actually くつ(kun) with 連濁. Catching self-corrections like this during data entry demonstrates exactly the value of careful character-by-character verification. 靴 on reading is カ (as in 軍靴=ぐんか), not くつ.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends 額 chain: 額縁(がくぶち, 重箱), 金額(きんがく, 音音), 半額(はんがく, 音音). 額=ガク is always on.
entries.real_world_context: Shopping — '半額セール' (half-price sale). Retail, consumer situations.

characters.reading_note: On only — 茶 was imported with the concept.
On only.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Both characters on-only. Like 茶畑, 茶 forces on. Here, 碗 also has no kun, so classification is doubly constrained.
entries.real_world_context: Dining — '茶碗蒸し' (steamed egg custard), 'ご飯茶碗' (rice bowl). Daily food vocabulary.
entries.trap_note: Extends 茶 chain from 茶畑(重箱). 茶碗(音音) vs 茶畑(重箱) — same 茶=チャ, different classification because 碗=ワン(on only) vs 畑=はたけ(kun only). Characters with no reading choice (on-only or kun-only) simplify prediction.

characters.reading_note: エン(on) here. Contrasts with 額縁 where 縁=ふち(kun).
かわ → がわ via 連濁.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 重箱 fill. Also extends 縁 chain: エン(on) here vs ふち(kun) in 額縁. Different readings, different meanings.
entries.real_world_context: Traditional houses, ryokan — '縁側でお茶を飲む' (drink tea on the veranda). Also sushi: 縁側 is a cut of fish.
entries.trap_note: 縁 reading contrast: エン(on, connection/veranda) in 縁側 vs ふち(kun, edge/rim) in 額縁. Semantic domain determines reading.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends 新 chain: 新芽(しんめ, 重箱), 新手(あらて, 訓訓), 新聞(しんぶん, 音音). Three classifications for one character.
entries.real_world_context: Daily life — '新聞を読む.'
entries.trap_note: 新 chain now has three classifications: 新聞(しん, on, 音音), 新芽(しん, on, 重箱), 新手(あら, kun, 訓訓). 新=シン in formal/abstract contexts, 新=あら in native/literary contexts.

characters.reading_note: 駅 has no standard kun reading.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Transportation vocabulary. 駅 is on-only, constraining any compound with it.
entries.real_world_context: Train travel — '各駅停車' (local train / stops at every station). Daily commuting vocabulary.
entries.trap_note: 駅 is on-only, so any X+駅 compound has the second element locked to on. 各駅(音音), 終着駅(しゅうちゃくえき, 音音). Structural constraint.

characters.reading_note: On only.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 重箱 fill. 茶 forces on; 色=いろ is kun here. Also starts a color-compound sub-pattern.
entries.real_world_context: Description, shopping — '茶色い犬' (brown dog). Daily color vocabulary.
entries.trap_note: 茶 chain: 茶畑(重箱), 茶碗(音音), 茶色(重箱). 茶=チャ always on. Classification depends on partner: 畑(kun)→重箱, 碗(on)→音音, 色(kun)→重箱.

characters.reading_note: Actually, はい is the KUN reading of 灰. On reading is カイ. So this is 訓訓, not 重箱.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Classification trap. はい 'sounds' like it could be on (many on readings are short and end in い), but it's kun. Contrasts with 茶色(重箱) — similar structure, different classification.
entries.real_world_context: Colors — '灰色の空' (gray sky). Description, mood.
entries.trap_note: 灰=はい(kun) vs 茶=チャ(on): both 'feel' similarly Sino-Japanese to many learners, but 灰 has a kun reading はい while 茶 has no kun reading at all. This is the same trap as 場=ば — short readings that feel like on but are actually kun.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Food vocabulary anchor. Straightforward 音音.
entries.real_world_context: Daily life — '弁当を持ってきた' (brought a boxed lunch). Convenience stores, stations, schools.
entries.trap_note: Useful food-domain 音音 anchor alongside 茶碗. Menu-reading module would pull from both 音音 food terms and 訓訓 cooking-method terms.

characters.reading_note: 丼 reading is debated — ドン is used as a clipped on-like reading, though the character's origin is Japanese (国字-like). Classification is fuzzy.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 丼=ドン is a borderline case — neither clearly on nor kun. Food vocabulary where exact classification is less important than knowing the reading.
entries.real_world_context: Restaurants — 天丼, 牛丼(ぎゅうどん), 親子丼(おやこどん). The 丼 pattern is very productive in food vocabulary.
entries.trap_note: X+丼 food set: 天丼, 牛丼, 親子丼, カツ丼, 海鮮丼. All use ドン. The character 丼 is interesting because its classification is genuinely unclear — it may be a 国字 (no true on reading) or an imported character (ドン as on). Pragmatically, just learn ドン.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Common abstract 音音. 雑 has no kun reading — structural constraint.
entries.real_world_context: Travel, crowds — '混雑を避ける' (avoid crowds). Train stations, tourist spots, event planning.

alternate_readings.context: Formal/counting — '一人前' can be ひとりまえ or いちにんまえ depending on context.

characters.reading_note: ひと is standard kun of 一. So this may be classifiable as 訓訓 rather than 熟字訓.
り is NOT a standard reading of 人. This makes the compound partially irregular — one character decomposes, one doesn't.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Borderline case. 一=ひと is standard kun, but 人=り is non-standard. Partially decomposable — same issue as 果物(くだもの).
entries.real_world_context: Ubiquitous — '一人で行く' (go alone). Counting people, restaurant reservations.
entries.trap_note: 一人 and 二人 are the only person-counters that use irregular readings. 三人(さんにん) onward is regular 音音. The り in ひとり/ふたり is an archaic counter that only survives in these two words. Knowing this boundary (1-2 irregular, 3+ regular) is immediately useful.

alternate_readings.context: Formal/counting contexts. '二人三脚(ににんさんきゃく)' (three-legged race) always uses ににん.

characters.reading_note: ふた is standard kun.
り is non-standard, same as 一人.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Pair with 一人. Same partial irregularity. Together they define the boundary of the irregular person-counter system.
entries.real_world_context: Daily life — '二人で食べに行こう' (let's go eat together, just the two of us). Reservations, seating.
entries.trap_note: 一人(ひとり)/二人(ふたり) = irregular. 三人(さんにん)/四人(よにん) onward = regular (mostly 音音). Exception: 四人 can be よにん(湯桶, よ=kun) or しにん(avoided due to homophony with 死人). The counter system is a 熟字訓 cluster with clear boundaries.

characters.reading_note: Actually, はつ is KUN not on. 初 on reading is ショ. So this is 訓訓, not 重箱.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Classification trap. はつ feels like an on reading (short, common in formal compounds: 初回, 初日) but is actually kun. Same trap as 場=ば.
entries.real_world_context: Conversation — '初耳だ!' (that's the first I've heard of it!). Surprise/news reaction.
entries.trap_note: 初=はつ is KUN despite appearing in many compounds that feel Sino-Japanese. Proof: 初 on reading is ショ (as in 初回=しょかい, 初期=しょき). When 初=はつ, it's always kun. This is another entry in the 'short readings ≠ automatically on' pattern: 場=ば, 気=キ(actually IS on), 初=はつ(kun), 灰=はい(kun).

alternate_readings.context: 初日の出(はつひので) = first sunrise of the year. はつひ reading is specific to this New Year's context.

characters.reading_note: ショ(on) here — the formal/event context triggers the on reading.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Dual reading with 初 shifting between はつ(kun) and ショ(on). しょにち = opening day (theater/events). はつひ = first day/sunrise (New Year's).
entries.real_world_context: Events — '初日の公演' (opening day performance). New Year's — '初日の出' (first sunrise).
entries.trap_note: 初 chain: 初耳(はつみみ, 訓訓, はつ=kun) vs 初日(しょにち, 音音, ショ=on). Same character, different reading/classification. はつ in casual/native compounds, ショ in formal/event compounds.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 重箱 fill. Common consumer vocabulary.
entries.real_world_context: Shopping, travel — '格安航空券' (discount airfare), '格安スマホ' (budget smartphone).

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends 毎X system with a clear 音音 example. 回=カイ(on) → 音音.
entries.real_world_context: Routine — '毎回遅刻する' (late every time).
entries.trap_note: 毎X system extension. 回=カイ is on → 音音. Further confirms the rule: classification depends on second character.

characters.reading_note: Single-character word. 峠 is a 国字 with only a kun reading. Not a compound — included to demonstrate 国字 as structural constraints.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Not a compound but a reference entry for 国字 constraints. 峠 in any compound locks that element to kun.
entries.real_world_context: Driving, geography — '峠を越える' (cross a mountain pass). Also figurative: '病気の峠を越えた' (got through the worst of the illness).
entries.trap_note: 国字 reference set: 畑(はたけ/はた, kun only), 込(こむ/こめる, kun only), 峠(とうげ, kun only), 辻(つじ, kun only), 枠(わく, kun only). Any compound containing a 国字 has that element locked to kun. This structurally eliminates certain classification possibilities.

characters.reading_note: 国字 — kun only.
くみ → ぐみ via 連濁.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 国字 + native noun = 訓訓 by structural constraint. 枠 can only be kun.
entries.real_world_context: Business/policy — '枠組みを作る' (create a framework). Strategic discussions, regulatory contexts.
entries.trap_note: 枠(国字, kun only) + 組(kun here) = 訓訓. If paired with an on-only partner, it would force 湯桶. 国字 entries are useful structural anchors — they remove ambiguity from one side of the classification.

characters.reading_note: 国字 — kun only.
褄 also has no standard on reading — rare character essentially limited to this compound and kimono terminology.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Both characters are kun-only. Double structural constraint → can only be 訓訓.
entries.real_world_context: Business/logic — '辻褄が合わない' (doesn't add up / the story doesn't make sense). Very common expression.
entries.trap_note: Two kun-only characters can only produce 訓訓. This is the strongest structural constraint — zero classification ambiguity. Rare in practice but demonstrates the principle.

characters.reading_note: かえ → がえ via 連濁.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 重箱 fill. Common practical vocabulary. Also extends 替 chain from 代替.
entries.real_world_context: Travel, banking — '両替所はどこですか' (where is the currency exchange?). Airports, banks, convenience stores.
entries.trap_note: 替 chain: 代替(だいたい, 音音, 替=タイ on) vs 両替(りょうがえ, 重箱, 替=かえ→がえ kun). Same character, different reading based on compound context.

characters.reading_note: シ(on) here — contrasts with 手紙(てがみ) where 紙=かみ→がみ(kun).

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends 紙 chain: 手紙(かみ→がみ, kun, 訓訓) vs 表紙(シ, on, 音音). Same character, different reading.
entries.real_world_context: Publishing, documents — '表紙のデザイン' (cover design). Books, reports, presentations.
entries.trap_note: 紙 chain: 手紙(かみ/がみ, kun) vs 表紙(シ, on). Partner character determines reading: native て(kun) pulls かみ(kun), Sino-Japanese ヒョウ(on) pulls シ(on). The formality alignment heuristic works here.

characters.reading_note: 員 has no standard kun reading. On-only constraint.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Structural anchor. 員 is on-only. Any X+員 compound has the second element locked to on: 全員, 会員, 社員, 店員, 駅員.
entries.real_world_context: Business, groups — '全員参加' (everyone participates). Meetings, events.
entries.trap_note: 員(on-only) joins 駅, 碗, 雑 as characters that constrain classification. The X+員 set is productive: 会員(かいいん), 社員(しゃいん), 店員(てんいん), 駅員(えきいん) — all 音音 because both elements must be on.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 一=ひと(kun) in casual/concrete contexts. Contrasts with 一段落(いちだんらく) where 一=イチ(on).
entries.real_world_context: Food, tasting — '一口ちょうだい' (let me have a bite). '一口サイズ' (bite-sized).
entries.trap_note: 一 reading: ひと(kun) in concrete/countable contexts (一口, 一人, 一言), イチ(on) in abstract/formal contexts (一段落, 一般, 一瞬). Semantic-formality split applies.

alternate_readings.context: More formal/emphatic — '一言もない' (I have nothing to say). Weight and finality.

characters.reading_note: こと is a kun reading meaning 'word' — not to be confused with 事=こと.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Dual reading with nuance split. ひとこと(casual, concrete one word) vs いちごん(formal, emphatic). Same 一 pattern as 一口.
entries.real_world_context: Conversation — '一言いいですか' (can I say one thing?). Also '一言多い' (you talk too much / one word too many).
entries.trap_note: 一 chain: 一口(ひとくち, 訓訓), 一言(ひとこと/いちごん, 訓訓/音音), 一人(ひとり, 熟字訓), 一日(ついたち, 熟字訓), 一段落(いちだんらく, 音音). Five entries showing the full range of 一's behavior.

characters.reading_note: ね(kun) — the 'price' meaning. 値=チ(on) in 価値(かち).

entries.difficulty_rationale: Common word. 値=ね(kun) for 'price' meaning is distinct from 値=チ(on) for 'value' (more abstract).
entries.real_world_context: Shopping — '値段はいくらですか' (what's the price?). Consumer situations.
entries.trap_note: 値 semantic split: ね(kun) = price/concrete (値段, 値札, 値引き) vs チ(on) = value/abstract (価値, 数値). Reliable prediction heuristic.

characters.reading_note: フ → ぶ (voicing). This is sequential voicing, not 連濁 strictly — it occurs between two on readings.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Common word. Straightforward 音音.
entries.real_world_context: Sports, games, competition — '勝負だ!' (it's a match!/game on!). Also '真剣勝負' (serious showdown).

characters.reading_note: Always ゆう(kun). Extends 夕 chain.
くれ → ぐれ via 連濁. 連用形 of くれる.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends 夕 chain. 夕=ゆう(kun) consistently across 夕刊, 夕食, 夕飯, 夕暮れ.
entries.real_world_context: Literary, daily life — '夕暮れ時' (twilight hour). Atmospheric description.
entries.trap_note: 夕 chain: 夕刊(湯桶), 夕食(湯桶), 夕飯(湯桶), 夕暮れ(訓訓). 夕=ゆう is always kun — four entries, zero exceptions. One of the most reliable anchors in the dataset.

characters.reading_note: よみ is the 連用形 stem of よむ.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Meta entry — the word 音読み itself is 重箱読み. And 訓読み(くんよみ) is 訓訓読み. Delightful self-reference.
entries.real_world_context: This tool itself. The terminology learners use to discuss reading types is itself an example of those reading types.
entries.trap_note: 音読み is 重箱読み. 訓読み is 訓訓. 重箱読み is 重箱読み (重=ジュウ on, 箱=ばこ kun). 湯桶読み is 湯桶読み (湯=ゆ kun, 桶=トウ... wait, 桶=おけ is kun, so 湯桶 is actually 訓訓, not 湯桶). This meta-recursion is worth one drill question for the sheer delight of it.

characters.reading_note: クン is the ON reading. Ironic: the word for 'kun-reading' uses the on reading of 訓.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Another meta entry. 訓読み (the word for kun-reading) is actually 重箱読み (on+kun), not 訓訓 as you might expect.
entries.real_world_context: Linguistic discussion, this tool's own terminology.
entries.trap_note: The beautiful irony: 訓読み is itself 重箱読み, not 訓訓. 訓=クン is ON (the on reading happens to sound like 'kun'). This is a perfect trick question for the classification drill.
